effects: The maintainers tree is treated as a governed third-party source depot rather than a social roster or recursive dependency mirror.
Each admitted package receives an independently inspectable governance record even when packages share an upstream organization.
Each package declares an upstream tracking channel, and Vaporize refreshes the newest eligible candidate independently of the revision admitted to consumers.
Vaporize owns read-only inventory, source collision detection, compatibility cohorts, advancement proof, and retirement proof.
Local modifications are modeled as bounded light forks with exact upstream bases, patch budgets, verification matrices, and exit conditions.
Multiple versions require explicit cohort-level exceptions and never imply that one SwiftPM leaf graph can load two versions of one identity.
followUps: Define and validate the governed package record schema.
Add a read-only Vaporize depot inventory command before any mutation command.
Add automated depot refresh, freshness status, and stale-candidate diagnostics with a declared freshness service level.
Use swiftlang/swift-subprocess as the north-star package for continuous upstream freshness, identity convergence, consumer inventory, and gated adoption.
Materialize Swiftly as the first light-fork fixture without sealing its current working-tree candidate.
Add compatibility-cohort and multiple-version-exception records after inventory truth is proven.
Require receipts for admission, advancement, patch rebase, and retirement workflows.
rationale: Package managers solve leaf resolution but do not provide fleet-wide source authority, patch, consumer, or retirement governance.
Organization directories are useful provenance groups but are too broad to be dependency approval boundaries.
Recursively admitting every transitive dependency would allow the resolver graph to define substrate ontology and create unbounded false ownership.
The existing MaintainerSwiftPMConfiguration already establishes Vaporize as the operational authority for mirrors and editable maintainer checkouts.
A small explicit fork is cheaper to operate than hidden working-tree divergence when its base, budget, proof, and exit are durable.
summary: Accept a Google-style governed third-party package depot, operated by Vaporize, with fresh upstream candidates, gated consumer adoption, package-level records, non-recursive admission, explicit light forks, and bounded multiple-version exceptions.
title: Govern third-party source as a package depot
